title: Security review: encryption & KMS (BYOK/HSM)
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked FinCore through encryption architecture options for hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Main discussion focused on customer-managed key (BYOK) patterns, HSM import/unwrap, envelope encryption, key rotation, and audit logging. Action items include sending SOC 2 report, encryption whitepaper, and scheduling a technical deep dive to validate BYOK flow in a Private deployment and a short proof-of-concept for key import and rotation tests.
action_items: Alex Chen - send SOC 2 Type II report, encryption whitepaper, and SOC/ISO attestation links - 2025-11-15
Priya Nair - schedule a technical deep dive/poC for BYOK/HSM integration and provide runbook for key rotation - 2025-11-20
Jasper Lee (FinCore) - share current KMS provider details, key policies, and compliance questions - 2025-11-18
Maya Patel - confirm data residency constraints and provide list of restricted regions - 2025-11-17
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 report and encryption whitepaper
Schedule technical deep dive for BYOK/HSM import flow
Set up short PoC to validate key rotation and audit logs in Redwood Private
Customer to provide KMS configuration and residency requirements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13, Start: 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (FinCore CISO), Daniel Kim (FinCore CTO), Renee Alvarez (FinCore Cloud Infra), Jasper Lee (FinCore SecEng), Omar Sheikh (FinCore Legal - joined late)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time today, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the account lead. we also have priya our solutions engineer and sam from customer success.
[00:10] Maya Patel: hi thanks, Maya here. we wanted to focus today's session on encryption requirements — at rest, in transit, and specifically on BYOK/HSM options, key rotation, and auditability.
[00:20] Daniel Kim: yeah we have upcoming regulator review and want to be sure our inference data does not leak and keys are under our control.
[00:30] Priya Nair: great, today we’ll cover the supported key management patterns across our Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, how envelope encryption works, hardware-backed keys, and audit logs. we'll also note caveats and what needs to be part of the PoC.
[00:45] Jasper Lee: quick Q — does Redwood offer a bring-your-own-key flow for hosted? or is BYOK only for Private?
[00:55] Alex Chen: short answer: for fully hosted public API we typically offer server-side managed keys, but we have a BYOK pattern for Dedicated in many enterprise contracts and full BYOK/HSM for Private deployments. there are some nuances, so priya will walk the flows.
[01:10] Priya Nair: ok so high-level, two patterns: envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS (CMEK/BYOK) where Redwood encrypts data with a data key and that data key is wrapped by a customer key in their KMS; and full key import into an HSM for Private where keys never leave your HSM. envelope is most common—less friction and still gives you control via KMS policies and key rotation.
[01:35] Renee Alvarez: when you say 'data key', is that ephemeral per-request or per-batch? what's the lifetime?
[01:45] Priya Nair: good q — we generate ephemeral data keys at session/batch granularity depending on workload. typical approach: per-tenant data key cached for short TTL (minutes) to avoid latency penalty; for low-latency streams we can use tighter caching with strict cache eviction and rotate per hour or on deploy.
[02:10] Jasper Lee: we also need attestable HSM-backed keys for the regulator — can you import keys into an HSM that Redwood manages or do we need to bring our own HSM?
[02:20] Alex Chen: in Redwood Private we support both: customer-managed HSM (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM like AWS CloudHSM) where you keep control; or we can integrate with your cloud KMS where you hold the root key material. for Dedicated contracts we offer integration with your KMS but the HSM import path is usually part of Private.
[02:40] Maya Patel: ok, regulator said they want key ownership demonstration, rotation history, and tamper-evident logs. how do we get those logs?
[02:50] Priya Nair: we emit KMS audit events and Redwood audit logs. for example, when a wrapped key is unwrapped for a data key operation we log, with request id, principal, and timestamp. those logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (splunk, sumo, or cloud logging). we can also provide signed audit bundles under NDA for attestations.
[03:20] Daniel Kim: are those logs stored in Redwood or streamed to our logging account? we're careful about retaining minimal PII in logs.
[03:30] Priya Nair: configurable — options: (1) default: events in our control plane for operations with redacted sensitive fields, (2) forward-only: stream all audit events to your logging endpoint over TLS, (3) private: in Redwood Private you keep logs in your VPC or local stack. we can redact token content and only include metadata.
[03:55] Jasper Lee: encryption at rest — do you use AES-GCM? what's the ciphersuite?
[04:05] Priya Nair: yes AES-256-GCM for data-at-rest; TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit. keys are wrapped using the cloud KMS standard wrapping algorithm (RSA-OAEP or AES-KW depending on provider). we also support HKDF-derived keys for session keys.
[04:30] Maya Patel: any FIPS requirements? our environment needs FIPS 140-2 validated crypto for certain keys.
[04:40] Alex Chen: Redwood can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs if you provide that; our Private deployment can run on FIPS modules. for hosted we rely on cloud provider FIPS options — we can document which components are FIPS-compliant.
[04:58] [01:00] Alex Chen (interruption): Omar — did legal join?
[05:00] Omar Sheikh: yes just jumped in, sorry had another call, can you recap key legal controls we should expect?
[05:10] Alex Chen: sure — we'll send the encryption whitepaper, SOC 2 Type II report, and an excerpt of our contractual security addendum. key points: customer owns KMS keys under BYOK, Redwood processes wrapped keys and does not persist unwrapped key material in control plane for Private deployments; audit logs and access policies are available for review.
[05:35] Daniel Kim: about key rotation — can Redwood rotate data keys and leave root keys at our KMS? how are versions handled if we rotate too often?
[05:45] Priya Nair: we recommend customer perform root key rotations in KMS and Redwood will rewrap or re-encrypt as needed. Data key rotation is layered: we rotate ephemeral data keys frequently and have a rewrap process for existing ciphertext if you change root keys — we provide a migration tool as part of the Private PoC. frequent rotation increases compute overhead so we'll profile during PoC.
[06:20] Maya Patel: if we revoke a key in our KMS, will Redwood immediately reject decrypt attempts? we need hard revoke semantics for breaches.
[06:30] Priya Nair: revoke in KMS causes subsequent unwrap attempts to fail, yes. we also support short TTL caching and can configure immediate cache invalidation hooks for Dedicated/Private so revoke is effectively immediate. for hosted, with server-managed caches there is a short window; for strict controls choose Private.
[06:55] Jasper Lee: can you walk through a sample flow — client sends data to Redwood, data encrypted at rest, which keys are used and where?
[07:05] Priya Nair: sure. sample: (1) client request arrives over TLS -> (2) Redwood runtime requests ephemeral data key (generated locally or fetched/wrapped) -> (3) data encrypted by runtime with data key -> (4) data key is wrapped by customer key in KMS -> (5) ciphertext stored; unwrap requires KMS decrypt/unwrapping to produce data key for read-time. for streaming generation we keep ephemeral keys cached for very short periods to avoid latency.
[07:40] Daniel Kim: for inference cache/kv cache — is the cache encrypted with the same data key scheme?
[07:50] Priya Nair: yes caches and KV cache are under the same envelope. in Private deployments you can choose to store KV cache in your VPC and control the encryption at rest there.
[08:05] Maya Patel: backups? snapshots? if you have snapshots of model state or logs, how are those protected and who controls encryption?
[08:15] Priya Nair: snapshots are encrypted using the same envelope approach; for Private snapshots remain in your network; for Dedicated we can encrypt snapshots using your KMS. backups of control-plane logs are segregated and access-controlled; we can provide retention settings as part of the contract.
[08:35] Alex Chen: can i ask about compliance timeline — you mentioned regulator review — what timing are we targeting for demonstrable controls?
[08:45] Maya Patel: we need evidence in 6 weeks, with technical evidence in 8-10 weeks. so a quick PoC then full roll out.
[08:55] Priya Nair: sounds tight but doable — PoC for BYOK import and rotation should be 2-3 weeks once we get KMS details and a small test dataset.
[09:10] Jasper Lee: we use AWS KMS and occasionally HashiCorp Vault for some internal services. for Vault we've got auto-rotate and HSM backends. can Redwood integrate with Vault's transit engine?
[09:25] Priya Nair: yes we have a Vault integration pattern — we treat Vault as the KMS provider for wrapping/unwrapping; there is an adapter in Private that handles session tokens and TTL, ideally deployed in your network. we'll need to test auth methods (AppRole vs IAM) during the PoC.
[09:50] Daniel Kim: what about key import format — do you support importing raw key material into a cloud HSM or do you need wrapped keys?
[09:58] Priya Nair: cloud HSMs generally support import via wrapped key blobs. for on-prem HSMs we can coordinate PKCS#11 import; for AWS CloudHSM you can generate keys in HSM or import a wrapped key. Private deployment gives the most flexibility.
[10:20] Maya Patel: is there any scenario where plaintext keys are handled by Redwood outside our KMS? that's a blocker for us.
[10:30] Alex Chen: short answer: no for BYOK in Private — Redwood does not persist unwrapped root key material. during unwrap operations the runtime may load ephemeral unwrapped data key into memory for crypto ops, but that is ephemeral and not written to disk. we'll document memory handling and secrets zeroization in the whitepaper.
[10:55] Jasper Lee: curious about HSM attestation — can you provide attestation statements from Redwood-managed HSMs?
[11:05] Priya Nair: attestation depends on provider. if you're using your own CloudHSM or on-prem HSM you control attestation. for Redwood-managed HSM we can provide provider-signed certs and logs but for strict regulator requirements we recommend customer-managed HSM.
[11:25] [12:00] Daniel Kim: any limitations for model weights encryption? we keep model artifacts encrypted at rest — do you re-encrypt when loading models for runtime?
[11:38] Priya Nair: model weights remain encrypted at rest; when loaded into GPU memory the runtime decrypts into memory for inference. we follow strict ephemeral memory policies and hold on to decrypted blobs only as long as needed. for extra assurance you can host models in your Private environment where you control the storage encryption.
[12:00] Maya Patel: about audit trails — do you log the actual KMS API responses or just metadata?
[12:10] Priya Nair: we log metadata: request id, operation type, principal, IP, timestamp, and outcome. we do not log raw plaintext keys or unwrapped key material. API response codes and error messages are logged. full request/response bodies are not retained unless explicitly configured for debug under NDA.
[12:40] Jasper Lee: what authentication methods do you support for KMS — IAM roles, service accounts, cert-based?
[12:48] Priya Nair: depends on provider — AWS: IAM roles; GCP: service accounts; Vault: AppRole or token; for on-prem PKCS#11 we use client certs. we'll enumerate details in the runbook.
[13:05] Alex Chen: can we talk about RBAC and SSO briefly — who has ability to request unwraps or call KMS in your model?
[13:15] Priya Nair: Redwood enforces RBAC: only runtime principals performing inference have unwrap permissions in our model; human users cannot trigger unwraps directly. admin ops can request key management ops which are gated by RBAC and MFA. in Private deployments you can map your SSO groups to Redwood roles with SAML/SCIM for fine-grained control.
[13:45] Maya Patel: we need separation of duties and privileged access reviews quarterly — is that supported?
[13:52] Alex Chen: yes we can provide access reports and integrate with your identity provider for central review.
[14:00] Jasper Lee: storing keys for multi-tenant — are keys per-customer isolated?
[14:08] Priya Nair: yes per-tenant keys and per-environment isolation. we don't share key material across tenants.
[14:20] Daniel Kim: what about replication across regions — if we replicate storage, do we replicate wrapped keys too?
[14:28] Priya Nair: we replicate ciphertext; wrapped keys can be rewrapped in the destination region using a regional KMS key. we can also choose to use a multi-region key in your KMS. for data residency constraints we keep rewrapped keys only in allowed regions.
[14:50] Maya Patel: ok can we get a short demo or diagram of the key flow?
[14:58] Priya Nair: yes i'll send architecture diagrams and a step-by-step flow.
[15:05] Sam Ortiz: one note — we recently ran a Dedicated customer PoC with a similar requirement and documented latency impacts; i'll attach that benchmark.
[15:15] Daniel Kim: what's the typical latency hit for unwrap ops with external KMS?
[15:22] Priya Nair: unwrap is ~50-200ms depending on KMS and network; with caching of ephemeral data keys you can amortize that cost. in Dedicated/Private where KMS is in same VPC/region it typically sits at the lower end.
[15:40] Jasper Lee: do you support HSM key rotation policy automation? we want scheduled rotations with proof.
[15:48] Priya Nair: yes we can orchestrate rotation triggers and produce rotation audit trails; the actual rotation is executed in your KMS if you host it. Redwood can trigger rewrap/migration workflows and provide a signed rotation report.
[16:10] Maya Patel: about encryption algorithms — any legacy ciphers used anywhere? we require no deprecated algorithms in our stack.
[16:18] Priya Nair: no deprecated ciphers; everything uses modern AES-GCM/TLS1.2+ with secure key lengths. we'll provide cipher lists in the whitepaper.
[16:35] Jasper Lee: can the PoC include a simulated key compromise and demonstration of revoke and re-encrypt? we want to see how fast we can quarantine and recover.
[16:45] Priya Nair: yes we can run that scenario in the PoC: revoke key, validate unwrap failures, re-encrypt and restore service. we'll test cache invalidation and failover behaviors.
[17:05] Daniel Kim: does Redwood provide a dedicated KMS proxy or do we need to open outbound to your control plane?
[17:12] Priya Nair: for Private we deploy a KMS connector inside your VPC which talks to your KMS and the Redwood runtime over private networking. for Dedicated we can also use a connector; hosted may require secure outbound to the KMS endpoint. connectors reduce surface area.
[17:40] Maya Patel: legal question — do you have contract language to specify key ownership and breach responsibilities?
[17:48] Alex Chen: yes we have a security addendum that specifies key ownership, responsibilities, breach notification timelines, and indemnities. we'll share a redlineable doc.
[18:05] Jasper Lee: are there examples of customers doing BYOK with Vault and CloudHSM we can reference?
[18:13] Alex Chen: yes i'll share anonymized case studies and a short runbook. Sam will include the benchmark and a PoC template.
[18:30] [19:00] Daniel Kim: one more on data residency — we have EU PII that must remain in eu-west-1; can Redwood ensure keys and ciphertext never leave region?
[18:45] Priya Nair: yes we support region-scoped KMS keys and storage. in Private we can restrict network egress. for Hosted/Dedicated we have region routing policies; we'll need to confirm endpoints for eu-west-1.
[19:05] Maya Patel: ok thanks. Omar anything on legal side?
[19:10] Omar Sheikh: i'll need the addendum and SOC 2; also confirm indemnity language around crypto failure — i'll follow up via the doc share.
[19:25] Alex Chen: noted — we'll include that.
[19:30] Priya Nair: to wrap up i'll summarize PoC scope: 1) validate BYOK unwrap/wrap with AWS KMS and Vault; 2) test HSM import path in Private; 3) run revoke/re-encrypt scenario; 4) produce audit bundles and rotation proof. estimate 2-3 weeks for initial PoC.
[19:55] Maya Patel: sounds good. can you also include expected costs for Dedicated vs Private for this setup? we need ballpark figures for budgeting.
[20:05] Alex Chen: yes i'll send estimated TCO and cost impact of rotation frequency and KMS API calls. Sam will include previous benchmark numbers.
[20:20] Jasper Lee: one minor follow — are debug logs accessible? sometimes we need deeper traces for security reviews.
[20:30] Priya Nair: accessible under NDA and gated by RBAC; debug logs may contain sensitive information so we only expose them for specific investigations.
[20:45] Daniel Kim: ok that's helpful.
[21:00] [22:00] Alex Chen: i'll recap next steps — share SOC2 and whitepaper, schedule technical deep dive, collect KMS details, and run PoC.
[21:20] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll get KMS info and region list by Monday.
[21:30] Omar Sheikh: thanks all, will look at addendum and get back with redlines.
[21:40] Alex Chen: thanks, meeting adjourned.
